Project Status is now Theta Θ

I got a PM asking what the prior Status of Epsilon meant a while back, so
I'll explain development phases in case anyone is interested as to what such
terms mean -- at least in my projects, YMMV.

Most people are familiar with the Alpha and Beta stages of software development.
Alpha is somewhat experimental and in flux, may not yet be fully functional.
Beta phase usually means the project is functional but needs testing / polishing.
Most devs tend to define these terms rather loosely making it hard for outsiders
to make sense of their meaning. Such is the nature of the beast. In Alpha and
Beta phases the software generally has version numbers and is working towards a
fairly clearly defined goal, often following a road map and/or completing feature
lists.

In my projects there is also ( Δ ) Delta which comes after Beta. Delta in
mathematics usually quantifies differences. Delta phase in software means a
functional product which receives patches. Patches are basically incremental
differences, hence Delta.

( Ω ) Omega comes after Delta phase and is the end of life for the project. Some
would reason then that the product cycle goes from Alpha to Omega. However, the
terms Alpha and Beta were haphazardly chosen by devs who didn't formalize the
full production cycle. They use terms such as "R&D" and "preproduction" for
phases prior to Alpha. Alpha to Omega doesn't encompass all of a product's cycle.

We're now leaving ( ε ) Epsilon phase. In statistics Epsilon usually has to do
with error allowances, or the system's tolerance for chaos. In my dev parlance
Epsilon phase is the initial chaotic research and prototyping done to determine
the operating parameters of the system within which features may be
accomplished. One such parameter for this project is how much can be done
in limited CSS space. Individual features are experimented with during Epsilon
to demonstrate feasibility and discover how to implement and integrate them.
During Epsilon the product has no version, only a collection of possible "proof
of concept" features are gathered.

Prior to Epsilon a project is in ( Ψ ) Psi phase. During Psi a product is
merely ideas, ranging from private musings to napkin diagrams up to full design
documents. I chose the label Psi due to its common roots with terms like
Psionics, because devs who are designing at this phase without even knowing
what is possible to achieve on the system must have psychic powers otherwise
the end result will not match their dreams. In practice this early artistry
and conceptual phase contains mockups, concept art, elevator pitches, and
design treatments, sometimes even with fancy but misleading 3D rendered
graphics. It's a rule of thumb to avoid donating to a crowd-funded project if
it hasn't left the Psi phase of development.

Theta phase comes after Epsilon. In statistics Theta is a space of parameters
from which estimates are made or predictions can be formed. In software dev
lingo Theta represents the process of fitting together and fleshing out the
features which were determined during Epsilon. Multiple features are roughly
combined, tested and cataloged, the project remains in flux as the development
road map is determined. By the time Theta phase is complete properly versioned
Alpha development can being.

To summarize the product life cycle:

Ψ Psi: Concept and Design. General ideas of what to create.
ε Epsilon: Determine platform capabilities, partial prototypes.
Θ Theta: Develop a plan of attack based on INTEL gathered.
A Alpha: Solidify design & work towards a usable product.
B Beta: Test and polish the software, add bells and whistles.
Δ Delta: Maintain the software with incremental updates.
Ω Omega: End of life. Repeat at Psi for a new project or sequel.
Status Change: Theta. + Explanation of development phases.
